title: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys

learn.hook: Shh! Story time! Grandparents know the best old stories.
points: The lesson is a funny folk tale about a cap seller and some naughty monkeys.
A folk tale is an old story. People tell it again and again.
The people and animals in a story are its characters.
When we listen, we look at the speaker and stay quiet.
Here is our own story: Raju and the Bell.

example.q: Listen: "Raju had a shiny red bell. He sat under a neem tree to rest. Mini the monkey took the bell and climbed up the tree. Mini copies everything she sees. Raju had an idea. He clapped his hands. Mini clapped too! The bell fell down, and Raju picked it up." Who are the characters?
steps: Who is in the story? Raju is in it.
A monkey named Mini is in it.
So the characters are Raju and Mini.

learn.reallife: At bedtime, Nani or Dadi may tell us an old story they heard when they were small.

games.title: Raju and the Bell: true or false?
items: In the story, Raju had a red bell.
The story says: Raju had a shiny red bell.
In the story, Raju sat under a neem tree.
He sat under a neem tree to rest.
In the story, a cat took the bell.
Mini the monkey took the bell.
In the story, Mini copies what she sees.
The story says Mini copies everything she sees.
At the end of the story, the bell is lost.
The bell fell down and Raju picked it up.

quiz.q: Read: "Raju had a shiny red bell." What colour was the bell?
quiz.explain: The line says the bell was shiny and red.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the colour word

quiz.q: Read: "He sat under a neem tree to rest." Where did Raju sit?
quiz.explain: The line says he sat under a neem tree.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Read: "Mini the monkey took the bell." Who took the bell?
quiz.explain: The line says Mini the monkey took it.

options: An old story told again and again
quiz.explain: Folk tales are old stories passed on by people.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a folk tale is

quiz.q: How should we listen to a story?
quiz.explain: Good listeners stay quiet and look at the speaker.
quiz.mistake: Does not know good listening manners

quiz.q: Read: "Mini climbed up the tree." Climbed up means Mini went ___.

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a folk tale? Who was in our story?
teach.praise: What a lovely story! I want to hear it again!
teach.nudge: Who was in the story? What did they do?

learn.hook: Monkey see, monkey do! Can you copy a funny face?
points: To copy means to do the same thing as someone else.
In the lesson, the monkeys copy the cap seller.
Clever means quick at thinking of good ideas.
Raju was clever. He knew Mini would copy him.

example.q: Think it through: Raju clapped. Mini clapped too. Why did the bell fall?
steps: She copied Raju and clapped her hands.
To clap, she let go of the bell, so it fell.
example.answer: Mini let go of the bell to copy Raju's clap.

learn.reallife: When we play "Simon says" or "Follow the leader", we copy the leader.

quiz.q: Raju waves. Mini waves too. What is Mini doing?
quiz.explain: Doing the same as someone else is copying.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of copy

quiz.q: Which word means quick at thinking of good ideas?
quiz.explain: A clever person thinks of good ideas quickly.

quiz.q: Raju knew Mini copies everything. Then he clapped. Why did he clap?
options: He knew Mini would copy him
quiz.explain: Raju wanted Mini to copy him and drop the bell.
quiz.mistake: Misses the reason in the story

quiz.q: Which is the opposite of up?
Read: "Mini took the bell." The opposite of took is ___.
quiz.explain: Take and give are opposites. Took and gave are opposites too.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with a similar meaning

quiz.explain: Cap and map both end with the sound -ap.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first letters

teach.ask: Gappu: What does copy mean? Why was Raju clever?
teach.praise: Clever you! I will copy your good idea!
teach.nudge: What does it mean to copy someone?

learn.hook: Stories are like a train. Each part comes in its turn!
points: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
We use first, next, then and last to tell a story in order.
If we mix up the order, the story does not make sense.

example.q: Put in order: (a) The bell fell down. (b) Mini took the bell. (c) Raju clapped his hands.

learn.reallife: We get ready in order: first we wake up, then we brush, then we bathe, then we eat.

quiz.q: Story: Raju sat under a tree. Mini took the bell. The bell fell. Raju picked it up. What happened first?
quiz.explain: The story begins with Raju resting under a tree.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the beginning and the end

quiz.q: Story: Mini took the bell. Raju clapped. The bell fell. Raju picked it up. What happened last?
quiz.explain: At the end, the bell fell and Raju picked it up.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the beginning and the end

quiz.q: Raju clapped. Mini copies everything she sees. What did Mini do next?
options: Mini ran away with the bell
quiz.mistake: Does not follow the story order

quiz.q: Which word tells the end of a list of steps?
First I wake up. Next I brush my teeth. Then I ___.
quiz.explain: After waking and brushing, we eat breakfast.
quiz.mistake: Repeats a step or jumps to the end of the day

quiz.q: Which comes first in a story?
quiz.explain: A story starts with the beginning.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the parts of a story

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I tell a story in the right order?
teach.praise: First you taught me, then I learnt, and last I said thank you!
teach.nudge: Which words help us tell a story in order?
